content:
Looking to use Signal on multiple devices simultaneously? This encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to access the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, no longer limited to using only an iPad as a second mobile device.

In addition to announcing the Android linking feature today, the company stated: "We are expanding linked device support on iOS. In addition to iPad, which we have always supported, you can now also link an iPhone to your Signal account."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their complete message history, along with media files stored within the past 45 days.

Signal stated that the transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption and employs the same link-and-sync technology used for iPads and desktop devices, including Signal for Mac.

This expanded support is particularly useful for users who need two iPhones to separate work and personal matters, or for those who need to test multiple devices.

This move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to the Apple Messages ecosystem, allowing users to seamlessly continue conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal version 8.22 for iOS is coming soon to the App Store. Signal has also recently launched a username feature, allowing users to establish contacts without sharing their phone numbers.
